points.description: Explains that the new data point is compared with the existing labelled (classified/coloured) data and the k nearest data points around it are selected (the 'sphere' of k nearest neighbours). Equivalent wording such as 'find the k closest training examples' earns the mark.

Explains that the new point is assigned the class that receives the maximum vote among those k nearest neighbours (majority voting). Equivalent wording such as 'most common class among the neighbours' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Two marks, one per distinct idea: selecting the k nearest labelled points, then assigning the majority class by vote. Full marks for either idea stated clearly in the student's own words, even if no pseudocode is given, since the model answer contains none. Do not award marks for the phrase 'unsupervised manner' either way, because the model answer's wording on this is inaccurate and kNN is a supervised method. No partial credit is needed because each point is all-or-nothing.
